text:
I saw the dawn mist

slide its silver gestures,

move an opaline density

in that portico of dream.


At the border there was a dead horse.


Crystal grains rolled over

its clear flank: and some wind

made its mane, small,

an arabesque, a sad adornment


—and moved the dead horse’s tail.


The stars still lived

and had not yet been born

ah! the flowers of that day…


—but its body was a bed:


a garden of lilies, the dead horse.


Many travelers contemplated

the fluid music, the dew-covered

great emerald flies

arriving in a murmurous stream.


Ahead, sad, the dead horse.


And living horses were seen,

tall as slender ships,

galloping in the fine air,

with happy profiles of dream.


White and green the dead horse was seen,


in the immense, destitute field

—and slowly the world turned

between its eyelashes, dim

in the moons of purple mirror.


The sun struck the dead horse’s teeth.


But everyone was in great haste,

and did not feel how earth

and the league’s course lacked

the agile, immense, ethereal breath

that was missing from that frame.


So heavy, the dead horse’s chest!

translation.title: The Dead Horse
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the supplied Spanish version of a Portuguese original. Capitalization and unusual syntax in the source are normalized only where needed for English grammar.
